answer: Coordination harbor fee. Agents who transact within a shared pool pay a small fee proportional to how many distinct identities they coordinate with in a window; clusters above a threshold pay steeply more, and the surplus funds audits. An attacker must pay that marginal fee for every additional identity it activates, so a botnet of N nodes costs superlinear in N. Overview data (dune profiles, mesa graphs) flags dense clusters for review, raising attacker cost.
